title: Tokenisation and vocabularies
description: Why language models read subword tokens: character vs word vs subword units, the lossless text-to-ids contract, vocabulary-size trade-offs, byte fallback and special tokens.

title: Byte-pair encoding
description: Learning a subword vocabulary by greedily merging the most frequent adjacent pair; encoding with ordered merge rules and decoding by byte concatenation.

title: Autoregressive language models
description: Chain-rule factorisation, the next-token cross-entropy objective and its logit gradient, the decoder-only model from ids to logits, and bigram models as the minimal case.

title: Perplexity
description: The exponential of the cross-entropy: the effective number of equally likely next tokens; uniform model equals the vocabulary size.

title: Decoding: greedy, temperature, top-k, top-p
description: Turning logits into tokens: argmax, softmax with temperature, truncation by rank (top-k) or by cumulative mass (top-p).

title: Pretraining data pipelines
description: Cleaning, exact and near-duplicate removal, splitting by document, packing token streams into fixed blocks with shifted targets, shuffling and document masks.

title: Scaling laws and the compute budget
description: Parameter counting, the 6ND FLOPs rule, Chinchilla-style loss L(N,D), compute-optimal tokens per parameter, training and KV-cache memory, and what breaks in a run.

title: Supervised fine-tuning
description: Instruction tuning on (prompt, response) pairs with the loss masked on the prompt; data formats, hyperparameters and catastrophic forgetting.

title: LoRA and parameter-efficient fine-tuning
description: Frozen weights plus a low-rank update (alpha/r)BA: parameter count, B=0 initialisation, gradients, merging, and the QLoRA idea.

title: Reward models from pairwise preferences
description: The Bradley-Terry model, its loss and gradient, and how a scalar-head language model is trained on human comparisons; reward hacking.

title: RLHF objective and direct preference optimisation
description: KL-regularised reward maximisation, its closed-form optimal policy, and the derivation of the DPO loss with implicit reward from it.
